claims.claim: The victory of the Christian faith in the ancient world was largely driven by a reversal that promised immortality to those whose world was doomed, which simultaneously lowered the esteem and dignity of politics by reducing it to an activity subject to necessity.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Historically, it is more than probable that the victory of the Christian faith in the ancient world was largely due to this reversal, which brought hope to those who knew that their world was doomed, indeed a hope beyond hope, since the new message promised an immortality they never had dared to hope for. This reversal could not but be disastrous for the esteem and the dignity of politics.

claims.claim: Individual life replaced the body politic as the central entity holding the position once reserved for collective political immortality, ultimately establishing life on earth as the highest good of man.
claims.supporting_excerpt: It is precisely individual life which now came to occupy the position once held by the “life” of the body politic... only when the immortality of individual life became the central creed of Western mankind, that is, only with the rise of Christianity, did life on earth also become the highest good of man.

must_not_be_lost: The historical role of the Christian shift from worldly immortality to individual immortality.
The degradation of political activity from striving for worldly immortality to catering to necessity.
The emergence of earthly life as the highest good of man following the rise of Christianity.
output.segment_function: Examining the historical and theological roots of life as the highest good through the Christian shift toward individual immortality and its impact on politics and human existence.
